result.title: All roads lead to Markov kernel networks: A representation theorem for discretization-stable learning
result.summary: Operator learning seeks to approximate function-to-function maps in a way that remains stable when the input discretization changes, a property sometimes called "discretization invariance". We consider a quantitative refinement of this idea, called $\textit{uniform discretization stability}$, which builds on a common representation of input functions and their discretizations as probability measures and provides a Hölder bound relating output changes to the Wasserstein distance between these measures. Our main result is a representation theorem showing all uniformly discretization stable operators can be written exactly as a $\textit{stable Markov kernel network}$---an abstract architecture that is a joint generalization of transformers, Fourier neural operators (FNO), Flowers, and other successful learned operators. Our representation theorem characterizes a design space for discretization-stable operator learning; designing new architectures becomes a question of which parts of a Markov kernel network to parameterize, and how. We further show that the read kernels of these networks can be realized as solutions of regularized variational problems, with particular choices of costs and regularizers recovering the kernels of transformers, FNO, Flowers, their hybrids, and beyond. This variational formulation provides a systematic approach to architecture design, together with sufficient conditions for uniform discretization stability.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究算子学习的「一致离散化稳定性」，把输入函数及其离散化统一表示为概率测度，用 Wasserstein 距离给出输出变化的 Hölder 界，并证明此类算子可精确写成「稳定 Markov 核网络」，同时把读核刻画为正则化变分问题的解，从而统一 transformer、FNO 等架构。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以测度距离量化「输入离散化改变时输出是否稳定」的框架，可能为检验 LVR/VLM 中 latent 状态对图像分块、分辨率或 token 化变化的稳定性提供度量思路，并可核对注意力读核与变分形式的联系；但原文不涉及推理状态或视觉推理，迁移需自行判断。
